active_projects.description: Reduce or accept the Sapience extraction classifier cost now that extraction is metered. The classifier re-runs across the entire not-yet-extracted backlog on every run, which was free on the Ollama backend but is now the dominant per-run cost on the anthropic backend. A measured run took 29 minutes wall clock against only 3.5s CPU (entirely network-bound) to extract 71 sources and stage 1208 knowledge objects, with the classifier phase accounting for roughly the first 20 minutes before chunk extraction began. The Known gaps section of docs/sapience.md already records that the classifier classifies every not-yet-extracted session on every run while a backlog exists. Weigh the available levers: setting NO_CLASSIFY=1 (the vendor client comment is that redaction is the privacy guarantee, not this filter, at the cost of no longer filtering personal conversations out), caching classifier verdicts across runs the way source_skip verdicts are already cached in the source_rules.json state file, or accepting the cost and documenting it. Implement whichever is right and record the per-pass cost measurement in the Cost shape section of docs/sapience.md.

active_projects.description:
GOAL. Measure how much of this machine's session history Sapience actually captures, and decide
from that measurement whether to widen the extraction scope, raise the per-run chunk cap, put
extraction on a schedule, or leave the arrangement as it stands. The deliverable is a decision
grounded in collected numbers, not a configuration change chosen up front.

BASELINE STARTS AFTER TASK 138. Task 138 (`retire_machine_wide_sapience_surface`) rewrites
exactly what Sapience captures. Its owner-action instruction reconciles `~/.sapience/config.json`
so that `/home/benjamin/Projects/BimodalLogic`, `/home/benjamin/Philosophy/Papers/PossibleWorlds`
and `/home/benjamin/Projects/Logos/Verification` are set `enabled: false` for capture, so that
`/home/benjamin/Projects/abood` and `/home/benjamin/Projects/Sapience/sapience-app` are added as
enabled entries, and so that the top-level `folders` allowlist is reduced to the
transcript-directory keys of the four repositories that actually load the sapience extension.
That reconciliation changes the source population this task exists to measure. A coverage or
pending figure collected before it is applied characterises a corpus that is about to be
discarded, and any MAX_CHUNKS or coverage conclusion drawn from such a figure rests on the wrong
denominator. The measurement window therefore opens only once 138's reconciliation is applied on
disk; readings taken before that point are not usable as a baseline. Record in this task's
artifacts how the reconciliation was confirmed applied before the first reading was taken.

NOTHING EXTRACTS ON A SCHEDULE. `programs.sapience.backgroundSync` defaults to false and
`home.nix` does not set it, so no `sapience-sync.timer` is installed and nothing reads a
transcript unless asked -- see `docs/sapience.md`, "Nothing extracts on a schedule". The two ways
to run a pass are `sapience sync` in a terminal and `systemctl --user start
sapience-sync.service` for a detached run that logs to the journal. The measurement is therefore
a series of hand-run passes; there is no cadence to observe passively.

METHOD.

1. Measure the current backlog first, after 138 has landed. Run `sapience coverage` and record
   its "Available on disk" block verbatim: "would ingest now", "skipped (outside Nd window)",
   "skipped (headless/agent)", "skipped (subagent / harness-started transcripts)", "skipped
   (folder not chosen)", together with the "Per-run extraction cap: N chunks (MAX_CHUNKS)" line
   and the folders-selected line. Run `sapience pending` and record it too. These readings are
   the baseline; take the backlog size from this measurement rather than from any figure carried
   in from elsewhere.
2. Run at least five extraction passes by hand, spaced at least a day apart and spanning at least
   a week of ordinary work, so each pass has fresh transcripts to find and the drain rate is
   observable rather than inferred from a single run. Capture `sapience coverage` and `sapience
   pending` after every pass, along with that run's own skip counts.
3. After the series, review what the vault actually holds -- not only the counters. Read through
   `sapience review` output and spot-check that the captured material is substantive work rather
   than thread mechanics.

WHAT THE FILTERS DO. Two independent filters drop transcripts, and telling them apart is the
point of the measurement.

- An overridable interactivity predicate (`_interactive` in `~/.sapience/upload.py`) requires at
  least two DISTINCT substantive human turns -- each at least 20 characters and not beginning
  with `<`, `[` or `{`. Transcripts failing it are reported as "skipped (headless/agent)" and can
  be kept for a single run with `--include-agents` or `SAPIENCE_INCLUDE_HEADLESS=1`.
- A non-overridable rule (`source_skip` in the same file) classifies a transcript as `subagent`
  or `harness-started` and never reads it. The client says so outright: the skip message states
  that `SAPIENCE_INCLUDE_HEADLESS=1` does not override this. These appear in coverage output as
  "skipped (subagent / harness-started transcripts)".

On an orchestration-heavy workflow the second filter removes more than the first, so measured
coverage can fall far below the session counts the folder picker shows. `sapience coverage`
reports the two counts separately, and which one dominates drives the decision below.

THE CHUNK CAP. `MAX_CHUNKS` defaults to 50 per run (`~/.sapience/upload.py`,
`~/.sapience/extract_local.py`). Whether 50 chunks per hand-run pass drains the measured backlog
at a useful rate, or whether a wider pass is needed (`sapience backfill 365` raises the cap and
widens the window for one pass), is a question this task answers from the measured backlog.

CANDIDATE OUTCOMES. Any combination of these, or none:

- Add a `programs.sapience.includeAgentSessions` option wiring `SAPIENCE_INCLUDE_HEADLESS` into
  the sync unit, if the headless/agent skip count is large and that material proves worth
  keeping.
- Adjust the per-run chunk cap, or prescribe a periodic wider backfill pass, if 50 per pass
  cannot keep up with the measured backlog.
- Turn on `programs.sapience.backgroundSync` (with `syncInterval`, default "hourly") so
  extraction runs on a timer, if hand-running proves too easy to forget. This is one candidate
  outcome among several, weighed against the stated reason the default is false: extraction
  spends real money or CPU per run.
- Leave all three as they are.

This requires observation over time, not a one-shot change.

active_projects.title: Install claude-refresh timer via home-manager and make mako idle-Lean-tree prompts actionable
active_projects.description:
Install the claude-refresh hourly timer via home-manager and configure mako so its idle Lean LSP tree Kill/Keep prompts are actionable and do not auto-expire.

BACKGROUND. On 2026-09-15 /refresh found a 22h-idle Lean LSP process tree (lake serve -> lean --server -> 4-5 lean --worker) left alive by a still-open Logos/Theory Claude session; lean-lsp-mcp has no idle timeout. The agent-system side (~/.config/nvim, agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/claude-refresh.sh) is being reworked in sibling nvim tasks: PSS-based memory accounting (Pss_Anon + SwapPss via /proc/PID/smaps_rollup), CPU-delta idle tracking in ~/.local/state/claude-refresh/lean-trees.json, a 1 GB reclaimable-memory floor, and a desktop-notification prompt. The hourly run stays --dry-run; when a tree is idle >= 240 min AND >= 1 GB reclaimable it launches a detached `systemd-run --user --unit=claude-refresh-prompt-<rootpid>-<starttime>` that calls `notify-send -a claude-refresh -u critical -t 0 -A default=Kill ...`. Clicking (mako invoke-default-action) runs a re-verified targeted kill; dismissing snoozes 4h.

FINDINGS ON THIS HOST (measured 2026-09-15).
  - claude-refresh.timer is NOT installed at all (`systemctl --user list-timers` shows only claude-session-reaper.timer). The /refresh docs' "hourly cadence" therefore never runs here.
  - The generic unit shipped in ~/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core/systemd/claude-refresh.service sets `Environment=PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`, which is broken on NixOS (no procps/jq/gawk/notify-send/systemd-run there) and `User=%u` is invalid in a user unit.
  - modules/home/desktop/mako.nix sets default-timeout = 5000, which would auto-dismiss the prompt after 5 s (read as "Keep"), and no dmenu-style launcher exists for `makoctl menu`, so only the default action is clickable.

WORK.
  (a) New home-manager module modules/home/services/claude-refresh.nix modeled on services/claude-session-reaper.nix (oneshot service + calendar timer, OnCalendar=hourly, RandomizedDelaySec=300, Persistent=true). ExecStart = %h/.config/nvim/.claude/scripts/claude-refresh.sh --dry-run guarded by ConditionPathExists on the same path. Export a PATH containing ~/.nix-profile/bin and /run/current-system/sw/bin (procps, gawk, jq, coreutils, libnotify, systemd). The service must never end up `failed` (see the gmail-oauth2.nix precedent). Import it in modules/home/default.nix.
  (b) The service needs the graphical session's DBus for the spawned notification: ensure DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS / WAYLAND_DISPLAY reach the transient unit (systemd --user environment import under niri is the likely mechanism; verify, do not assume).
  (c) mako: add a criteria section for app-name=claude-refresh with default-timeout = 0 (and optionally a distinct border colour), keeping left-click = invoke-default-action and right-click = dismiss. Verify with `makoctl` and a real `notify-send -a claude-refresh -A default=Kill` round trip that the action name prints on click and nothing prints on dismiss.
  (d) Confirm the transient prompt unit name does not match `claude-*.scope`, so claude-session-reaper never stops it.

DEPENDENCY. The prompt-launching logic lands in the nvim-side notification-prompt task; (a), (c) and (d) can land first (the timer is useful for dry-run logging on its own), but end-to-end acceptance of (b) waits on it.

ACCEPTANCE.
  - After a home-manager switch, `systemctl --user list-timers` shows claude-refresh.timer; a manual `systemctl --user start claude-refresh.service` succeeds and journal output contains the Lean LSP pass report.
  - A notify-send with app-name claude-refresh stays on screen until clicked; click prints the default action, dismiss prints nothing.
  - No regression to claude-session-reaper or memory-monitor units.

Contain every Claude Code session in its own systemd user scope and reap abandoned scopes, so a detached child process can never outlive the session that spawned it. Root cause confirmed live: all claude sessions AND their children currently share one cgroup (app-gnome-org.wezfurlong.wezterm-3725.scope), so there is no per-session boundary to clean up. This produced a runaway `python3 -u search_world_bound.py` that survived its dead session for 2d3h, burned 50h47m of CPU, and held the package at 99C (k10temp Tctl) with the fan pinned at max; a parallel case leaked ~5GB of orphaned lean-lsp workers. Mechanism is empirically proven on this host, not assumed: (1) `systemd-run --user --scope --unit=claude-<id>` contains even a `setsid nohup` double-forked child in the scope cgroup -- verified by reading cgroup.procs; (2) `systemctl --user stop <scope>` SIGKILLs everything in it -- verified the escaped child died; (3) an abandoned scope is detectable by enumerating the scope cgroup.procs and finding no live process named `claude`. BINDING SAFETY CONSTRAINT (user-stated): the reaper MUST NOT interrupt long-running work the user legitimately wants. Therefore the reap predicate MUST be liveness-based ONLY -- "the claude session that owns this scope is gone" -- and MUST NOT use any CPU-time, memory, or wall-clock threshold as a kill criterion; a child running for hours must survive untouched as long as its owning session lives. The reaper MUST only ever act on units matching the claude scope naming pattern, MUST never touch a scope containing a live claude process, and MUST NOT enumerate or kill arbitrary user processes. Implementation surface: add the scope wrapper to packages/claude-code.nix (currently a thin `exec npx @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest`), verifying an interactive TTY session still works correctly inside a --scope; add a home-manager systemd user timer + service for the reaper; provide a documented opt-out for deliberately detaching work meant to outlive a session. Verify by launching a real claude session, confirming its children land in a distinct per-session cgroup, killing the session, and observing the orphan actually die -- never by inspecting unit files alone.

active_projects.description: Fix the battery-backstop wake-mark resume hook, which has never fired. battery-backstop-wake-mark.service declares only WantedBy=post-resume.target, but post-resume.target does not exist on this system (systemctl show reports LoadState=not-found and no matching unit file), so nothing ever pulls the unit in. Confirmed against a real suspend/resume cycle: ActiveEnterTimestamp empty, no /var/lib/battery-suspend-backstop/wake-mark file. Consequence: the backstop wake-grace window is permanently inert, so a wake at <=10% to plug in a charger is re-suspended within ~60s -- the exact HIGH-severity behavior the grace window was added to prevent. Two false proofs must not be repeated: the populated post-resume.target.wants/ directory is orphaned (systemd never loads a wants dir whose target unit is absent) and is not evidence of wiring, and the cited precedent disable-speaker-amp in audio.nix actually activates via multi-user.target at boot, not on resume. Rewire to a mechanism that exists here (After=/WantedBy=suspend.target, or powerManagement.resumeCommands -- powerManagement.enable is already true at modules/system/power.nix:122) and verify by an actual suspend/resume cycle producing a wake-mark file, never by inspecting .wants/ symlinks or by a test harness that writes the wake-mark itself

active_projects.description: Give the niri session AC/battery-conditional idle suspend (12h on AC, 1h on battery) to match the GNOME session. niri currently has zero idle auto-suspend on any power state (removed in task 117), and swayidle has no native AC/battery-conditional timeout: the single "timeout N command" clause spawned at config/config.kdl:271 applies unconditionally regardless of power source. Two candidate designs from the task 119 research: (Option A) a power-state-aware supervisor that respawns swayidle -w timeout <43200|3600> on /sys/class/power_supply/ACAD/online transitions, structurally mirroring the udev idiom already in modules/system/power.nix; (Option B) two mutually-exclusive systemd user units (swayidle-ac / swayidle-battery) gated on AC power. Known hazards either way: respawn races, two idle timers armed simultaneously, and a supervisor dying silently and leaving no idle policy at all. Must reuse the existing session-scoped systemd-inhibit mechanism from tasks 117/118 for Claude-activity awareness rather than building new detection. DO NOT resurrect the commented-out services.swayidle block in modules/home/desktop/swaylock.nix verbatim: its unconditional "timeout 600 -> systemctl suspend" example predates the AC/battery split requirement. Run the flake formatter over the whole tree and commit the resulting drift so the repo is fmt-clean, making future formatter output a no-op and keeping unrelated reflow out of unrelated content commits. The drift is confirmed, not hypothetical: a repo-wide `nix fmt .` run during the task-reference cleanup reflowed the `mkQuerymap` argument list in modules/home/email/aerc.nix from a single-line attrset pattern to the multi-line form, on a line nobody had edited. That hunk was deliberately reverted to keep the cleanup commit scoped, so the drift is still present in the tree. Other files very likely carry the same class of drift and were NEVER surveyed: the cleanup pass ran the formatter once and inspected the diff only for non-comment changes, so any file it did not otherwise touch went unchecked. Scope: run the formatter over the tree, then review the ENTIRE resulting diff hunk by hunk before committing. A formatter is not a licence to skip review -- confirm specifically that no string literal, heredoc, or embedded shell block inside a nix string had its content or semantics changed, since several modules under modules/home/email/ carry substantial shell scripts inside nix strings (mail-sync.nix, mbsync.nix) whose echo output is user-visible. Commit as a single formatting-only change with no content edits mixed in. Verification (all four required): a second formatter run after committing must produce ZERO further changes -- this idempotence check is the actual proof the tree is fmt-clean and must not be skipped; `nix flake check` must pass; `nixos-rebuild build --flake .#hamsa` must succeed; `home-manager build --flake .#benjamin` must succeed. Invocation caveat: the formatter is nixfmt 1.4.0 exposed via the flake `formatter` output, and invoking it as `nix fmt .` emits a deprecation warning that passing directories or non-Nix files is going away, recommending the pkgs.nixfmt-tree wrapper or treefmt-nix instead. Determine the intended invocation BEFORE scripting the sweep so the committed result matches what a future formatter run (and CI, if it ever checks) would produce -- otherwise the idempotence check will pass locally and drift will reappear. Finally, check whether CI enforces formatting at all: .github/workflows/ci.yml currently runs statix and deadnix but the tree was found already drifted, which suggests no fmt gate exists. Decide whether adding one belongs in this task or a follow-up, and say which.

roadmap_batches.description: Make the Sapience client declarative and stop the vendor re-wiring its machine-wide hooks
roadmap_batches.rationale:
Sapience leads this list now, and two of this batch's three members can genuinely be picked up today: 141 and 144 both carry an empty dependencies[] and sit in wave 1 on their own merits. 141 opens the batch because it is the convergence-and-detection half of the hook problem and because its scope (a) and (b) are the only work in the whole Sapience cluster that touches modules/home/core/dotfiles.nix -- the claudeSettings activation entry and its enforced-key list -- which 142's already-written plan explicitly declares out of its own scope. 144 follows: its three gaps (a sops-backed tokenFile, the sourceDirs registration decision, declarative lingering) are independent of the hook problem, and its own text already instructs the implementer to coordinate rather than duplicate should it reach the same activation entry; co-batching is what makes that instruction checkable instead of aspirational. 142 is listed last and wave dispatch will skip it until its recorded predecessor clears -- it stays in the batch regardless, because an unmet predecessor is an ordering constraint, never grounds for dropping a member, and because it shares docs/sapience.md and modules/home/services/sapience.nix with 144.

Two exclusions here are deliberate rather than overlooked, and are stated because a bare exclusion is indistinguishable from an oversight. First, no dependency edge is added between 141 and 142, even though 142's plan Phase 2 builds scripts/check-sapience-hooks.sh -- precisely the between-activations detector 141's own scope (c) still treats as an open siting question. The substantively correct direction would be 141-after-142, since 142's plan has already answered that siting question (detector in this repository, wired entryBefore ["claudeSettings"] so it reads live pre-merge state); but wiring that edge would park the one dispatchable task in this cluster behind 142, which is itself parked behind an owner-parked measurement. The ordering is therefore carried here in prose instead of in the graph: whoever takes 141 must read 142's plan Phase 2 and adopt its siting decision rather than build a second detector. Second, no edge is added between 144 and 142, 139 or 136 despite all four declaring docs/sapience.md, home.nix and modules/home/services/sapience.nix, for the same reason -- every would-be predecessor in that set is stalled behind the parked measurement, and an edge there would park dispatchable work behind something no task in this system can unblock.

roadmap_batches.rationale:
This pair sits second rather than first because neither member is attendable, and it is kept as a batch rather than dissolved so that neither task gets auto-suggested as ready work without this context attached. 136 is parked at the owner's request. Its status is deliberately unchanged -- it remains IMPLEMENTING, not held and not abandoned -- because parking here is an ordering signal about what to pick up next, not a lifecycle transition; its own shape already resists dispatch, since it is a series of five or more hand-run extraction passes spaced across more than a week, not something a single run can discharge. 139 is not merely sequenced after 136 by judgment, it is blocked behind it in the live graph, and that edge is kept rather than relaxed to make the batch look more actionable: 139's three levers -- NO_CLASSIFY=1, caching classifier verdicts the way source_skip verdicts are already cached, or accepting and documenting the cost -- can only be weighed against a measured backlog denominator that only 136 produces. 139's other recorded predecessor, the local-inference diagnosis, is now discharged, so 136 alone is what holds it.

This pair also carries the whole cluster's stall, which is why reopening the measurement window is worth more than it looks. 142's own edge onto 136 is the sole reason the lead batch's third member cannot dispatch, and that edge is a shared-territory serialization over docs/sapience.md, home.nix and modules/home/services/sapience.nix rather than a content dependency -- nothing in 142's plan reads a coverage figure or a backlog denominator. Reopening the window therefore unblocks two tasks, not one.

Running them together warms one context rather than two. No dependency edge is asserted between them: 131's own text states that its (a), (c) and (d) items can land first, and its only declared predecessor is a sibling task in the nvim repository, so co-membership here is ordering judgment, not evidence of a missing graph edge. One collision to keep visible: 131 item (c) adds a mako criteria section and 77 in the preceding batch also declares modules/home/desktop/mako.nix, so this batch running after that one is the right order -- reconcile the service behavior first, then add notification criteria on top.
